editorial.headline: Religious-Service Administration Is a Government Function
editorial.standfirst: This government activity supports religious guidance and harmony, but it is closed to foreign investment nationally and marked closed in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the administration of government services in religious affairs. Its remit is not a general commercial offering: it covers government work supporting Islam, Protestant Christianity, Catholicism, Hinduism, Buddhism and Confucianism, directed toward greater devotion to God Almighty and harmony among religious communities. Government institutions working in religious affairs are expressly within its scope. The practical character of the code is therefore public administration in a sensitive national sphere, defined by the work it performs rather than by a market-facing product or service.

The registration picture follows that public character. The record lists no business scales as open to this activity, and its national PMA status is TERTUTUP. The national foreign-ownership ceiling is 0%, leaving no foreign equity participation within the activity as recorded. That is the central fact for anyone assessing whether a foreign-investment structure can be used here: it cannot. For the national position, the cited source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not soften that conclusion. The Bali status is also TERTUTUP, and the record marks the activity as blocked for PMA registration. A foreign investor therefore cannot register this activity in Bali today. The reason supplied does not attribute the outcome to Bali’s island-wide moratorium: the record identifies the activity as medium-high/high risk and says it is not blocked by that moratorium, while directing verification for the particular address. That distinction is worth keeping clear. Bali’s stated moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently; this record instead preserves an address-verification point alongside its closed Bali outcome.

The clean reading is not that Bali creates an exception to an otherwise open national route. Nationally, the activity is closed, with a 0% foreign-ownership ceiling; in Bali, it remains marked closed and blocked for PMA. Its substance is the government administration of religious affairs and interfaith harmony, and the registration status follows the record’s treatment of that function. For a proposed Bali location, the only further operational instruction present in the record is to verify the position by address.
